column12: Judgement on the comparator. Kerendia is the closest marketed product in mechanism and setting: the only non-steroidal MR agent in the US, approved on 2025-07-11 (openFDA, NDA215341 efficacy supplement 9, in the book's supplements table; Bayer announced it on 2025-07-14, bayer.com/en/us/news-stories/fda-approves-kerendia) for heart failure with LVEF 40% or above to cut CV death, HF hospitalisation and urgent HF visits, and labelled in CKD with type 2 diabetes. One brand price, not two: AstraZeneca's existing dapagliflozin combination, Xigduo XR, reads $4,366 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 against Farxiga's $4,168 (1.05x), and every branded heart failure product on file sits close by: Farxiga $4,168, Jardiance $4,496, Verquvo $4,465, Entresto $5,055 (lookup.py demand, Part D 2024). Case for higher: a price at the sum of the two agents, Kerendia plus Farxiga, would be $8,661. Kerendia's per-beneficiary figure is also still rising with its ramp ($1,493, $2,857, $4,239, $4,493 over 2021 to 2024), so a part-year effect remains. Case against the revenue as incremental: BalanceD-HF compares against dapagliflozin, so the patients switch from a dapagliflozin regimen. While Farxiga is branded, part of this revenue is a transfer from Farxiga's line, which the book models separately. The book's Orange Book rows put dapagliflozin's US substance patent 7,919,598 at 2029-12-16, with the paediatric extension to 2030-06-16. After that the combination protects dapagliflozin revenue that would otherwise go generic. Not netted here.

column12: Judgement: the MRA rate is taken, not the SGLT2 inhibitor rate, because a patient who stops the MR component for potassium or kidney function stops the combination and returns to dapagliflozin alone. The setting matches BalanceD-HF's entry criterion, a recent heart failure event, and the data are US. Case against: a first-year rate applied to the whole stock every year overstates later-year stopping; 44.2% of steroidal MRA discontinuers restarted within a median 91 days in US claims (Richard EL et al., Pragmat Obs Res 2025;16:27-37, doi:10.2147/POR.S489791, PMID 40034401); and EVOLUTION HF pooled across Japan, Sweden and the US gives lower 12-month rates, 23.5% for dapagliflozin and 42.2% for MRAs (Savarese G et al., JACC Heart Fail 2023;11(1):1-14, doi:10.1016/j.jchf.2022.08.009, PMID 36202739). A single daily capsule may persist better than two pills

column11: Khera R et al., 'Temporal Trends in Heart Failure Incidence Among Medicare Beneficiaries Across Risk Factor Strata, 2011 to 2016', JAMA Netw Open 2020;3(10):e2022190, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.22190, PMID 33095250, PMC7584929. Results: in CMS's 5% sample of fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 and over, continuously enrolled in Parts A and B and free of heart failure, 'the incidence of HF decreased ... to 26.5 cases per 1000 beneficiaries (n = 37 620) in 2016'; incident HF is at least one inpatient HF claim or two outpatient HF claims in separate quarters. Methods: 'for every 100 individuals enrolled in Medicare, 5 are entered into the Medicare 5% sample'. 37,620 x 20 = 752,400 new diagnoses a year in fee-for-service Medicare aged 65 and over
column12: Population counted: new heart failure diagnoses in any setting, fee-for-service Medicare aged 65 and over, 2016. A lower bound on the national adult inflow: it leaves out Medicare Advantage enrollees and adults under 65, and 2016 is the latest year the paper counts (35.7 per 1,000 in 2011 falling to 26.5 in 2016). eligible_pct does not change. The engine passes incidence through the same eligible_pct as prevalence (forecast.patients_for_indication: incidence x eligible_pct x (1 + exus_multiple)), and this count measures what the book's 7.4mm measures, diagnosed heart failure, so the 0.17152 filter (event within 12 months, eGFR under 60) applies to it as it does to the prevalent pool. A first-hospitalisation count was the alternative and is not used: 2,634,645 incident heart failure hospitalisations in fee-for-service Medicare over 2014 to 2021, about 329,000 a year (J Card Fail 2025, doi:10.1016/j.cardfail.2025.12.006, PMID 41475614, abstract only). Those patients already meet the event criterion, so the engine would filter them for an event a second time (x 0.268), and one eligible_pct cannot be 0.64 for them and 0.17152 for the prevalent pool. It serves as a cross-check: about 44% of new diagnoses (329,000 over 752,400, different years) come through a hospitalisation, above the 26.8% event share applied, so the filter is conservative for new patients. The row is the asset's own, not the book's: epidemiology.csv leaves heart failure incidence blank, and assemble.py will copy this figure to any later heart failure asset. Engine consequence: untreated_carryover_pct is unset (1.0), so untreated eligible patients never leave by death. At the 0.0063 peak the engine's untreated eligible pool grows from 1.27mm to 2.45mm by year 10 (2038), against about 1.68mm at the same 0.17152 share of the book's own projected prevalence for 2038 (straight line from 8.7mm in 2030 to 11.4mm in 2050). The later-year pool is therefore overstated even with a lower-bound inflow. A carryover below 1.0 would correct it (1-year case fatality after a first acute decompensated heart failure admission is 29.5%, ARIC, PMID 24342763); not set here

column11: Two filters from BalanceD-HF's entry criteria (Saudi FDA trial summary, sfda.gov.sa/en/node/1387762). (1) A heart failure event: 26.8% of 16,646 US patients with chronic HFrEF had a worsening event, a heart failure hospitalisation or IV diuretics, within 12 months ('Clinical and Economic Burden of Chronic Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction Following a Worsening Heart Failure Event', Adv Ther 2020, doi:10.1007/s12325-020-01456-1, PMID 32761552, PMC7444407; IBM MarketScan, accessed by Merck, index year 2016). (2) eGFR under 60: 234,332 of 365,494 heart failure hospitalisations (64%) in GWTG-HF, 2014 to 2019 (Patel RB et al., 'Kidney Function and Outcomes in Patients Hospitalized With Heart Failure', J Am Coll Cardiol 2021;78(4):330-343, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2021.05.002, PMID 33989713). 0.268 x 0.64 = 0.17152, about 1.27mm of the book's 7.4mm
column12: The second share is measured among hospitalised patients, so it is already conditional on an event and the two multiply without an independence assumption. No ejection-fraction filter: the trial requires a recent LVEF reading but sets no cut-off. Case for lower: the trial requires the event within 6 months, not 12, and halving the first share gives 0.086. The 64% includes patients below eGFR 20, whom the trial excludes; the paper gives no count below 20, only a lower quartile of 34. The 26.8% comes from under-65 commercially insured HFrEF patients identified from claims, a sicker definition than the book's self-reported 7.4mm. Case for higher: older and HFpEF patients are hospitalised at least as often, and the label may drop the recent-event criterion, as the current US heart failure labels for Farxiga, Jardiance and Kerendia carry none. Verquvo's label does carry one (use following a heart failure hospitalisation or outpatient IV diuretics). Not applied: the trial also excludes current MRA users and requires NT-proBNP above 300 pg/mL, and a label would not restrict either

With this asset's 0.57 discontinuation and Kerendia's fitted curve (k 1.82, midpoint 0.58), the engine needs a peak of 0.0063 to reach 88,208 in year index 2, and it reproduces 18,001 and 55,240 for 2022 and 2023 against actual 25,931 and 63,625. Incidence is left at zero in the solve; adding 41% of the book's type 2 diabetes incidence gives 0.0055
column12: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0. Kerendia is the incumbent of the same prescribing decision: add a non-steroidal MR agent, with potassium monitoring, against generic spironolactone and eplerenone. Corroboration from the same setting: Verquvo, the branded add-on labelled for heart failure after a worsening event, had 11,127 Part D beneficiaries in 2024, its fourth year (lookup.py demand Verquvo). Over a pool of 7.4mm x 0.5 reduced ejection fraction (the book's epidemiology.csv note) x 26.8% with an event (PMID 32761552), the same solve gives 0.0074. Both numerators are Medicare Part D only, so both understate an all-payer capture. Case for higher: SGLT2 inhibitors were used by 12.0% of patients in the 12 months after a heart failure hospitalisation over June 2020 to September 2023 (EMPACE, PMID 41804888: 13% of HFrEF, 12% of HFmrEF and 9% of HFpEF, weighted by the cohort's 73/4/23 split). Solved as a year-3 treated stock that needs a peak of 0.10, but the reading overstates it twice. The 12.0% includes the 5.5% already on an SGLT2 inhibitor before the admission (5%, 7% and 7%), so new starts were 6.5 points, 6.9% of those not on one. And it is a one-year capture of a post-event cohort, which is what this peak measures, not a stock three years into a launch. The class figure is therefore 0.069, and it spans two heart failure brands: Farxiga held 32.7% of SGLT2 inhibitor Part D beneficiaries in 2024 (1,269,216 of 3,879,658 across Farxiga, Jardiance, Invokana and Steglatro, lookup.py demand), which puts one brand at about 0.023, 3.6 times this value. In the engine with this asset's incidence, year 5 treated US patients are about 19,000 at 0.0063, 67,000 at 0.023 and 252,000 at 0.10; the last is a fifth of Farxiga's whole 2024 Part D base and 2.9 times Kerendia's year-3 count. 0.0063 matches what the two single-brand incumbents measurably reached (Kerendia 0.80% of its pool by year 3; Verquvo 11,127 in year 4, 1.1% of its post-event pool) and stays, with 0.023 as the case for higher. Entresto held 795,291 Part D beneficiaries in 2024, 10.7% of the whole 7.4mm. AstraZeneca can also switch patients from its own Farxiga (1.27mm Part D beneficiaries in 2024, all indications) to one capsule, a channel Bayer did not have for Kerendia. Case for lower: finerenone will have been labelled in heart failure for three years by launch, and the MR component faces generic steroidal MRAs
